lots.guide_summary: Two SOLD entries, both close rather than the same item (English sterling pierced swing-handle baskets by other makers): AUD 378 for a 225g Birmingham basket and AUD 1,717 for a 578g Mappin & Webb. There are no UNSOLD or ASKING entries. Scaled to 362.2g, the weight-adjusted range is about AUD 609 to 1,086. Not a price paid, only a floor: 362.2g x 0.925 = 335g fine silver, and at spot USD 61.22/ozt (gold-api.com, 30 Sep 2026) that is about AUD 2.816/g, so melt is about AUD 943. A refiner pays less than full melt. Rates are from open.er-api.com, 30 Sep 2026: USD 1 = AUD 1.4308, CAD 1 = AUD 1.0085.
lots.working: There is no SOLD entry for the same item, so I weight-adjusted the close SOLD comps (silver baskets trade largely on weight). Lowest rate per gram: CAD 375 / 225g = CAD 1.667/g = AUD 1.681/g. x 362.2g = AUD 608.9. Keep: 608.9 / 1.198 = 508.3, rounded down to $505. Flip: resale AUD 609 less 13% selling fees (eBay-style) less $20 outbound postage = 509.8, / 2.396 = 212.8, rounded down to $210. The current bid is already $500 with 1 bid, so the flip route is gone and the keep ceiling is only just above it. A $505 hammer is $605 all in, well under the melt of about AUD 943. This ceiling is conservative because the comp dates from Nov 2025, when silver was cheaper.
lots.confidence_reason: The marks are read clearly (JD&S, Sheffield crown, lion passant, date letter n = Sheffield 1905-06), but the SOLD comps are close items rather than the same item, and they are weight-adjusted. I read them from LiveAuctioneers' data because the lot pages are blocked.
lots.dropped_entries: None. The researcher had no entries because the WebSearch budget was used up. The two SOLD entries above are my own additions from LiveAuctioneers data.
lots.key_photo_findings: Enlarged the base marks: JD&S in a shaped cartouche, crown, lion passant, and a lowercase gothic-style n in a cut-corner shield. That fits Sheffield 1905-06 and James Dixon & Sons, so the catalogue is confirmed. The handle is part-marked JD&S plus lion. Pierced vine frieze over vertical slots, gadrooned shaped rim, swing handle intact. Scratched initials 'AE' on the base.
lots.condition: Tarnished, with general surface scratching to the base and a dark oxidised patch on the handle plate. The rim may be slightly out of shape at one end (photo 6, not confirmed). No splits seen in the piercing at this resolution.
lots.question_for_gowans: Can you confirm there are no splits or repairs in the piercing or at the handle hinges, and whether the rim is bent? Is 362.2g the basket alone (no liner)?
